draft.title: Making a personal budget
card: A budget is a plan that lists the money you expect to receive (income) and the money you expect to spend (expenses) over a period, such as a month.
expenses that stay the same each time, such as a phone plan or a gym fee.
expenses that can go up or down, such as snacks, clothes or a myki top-up.
Subtract total expenses from income to see what is left to save. If expenses are higher than income, the budget shows a shortfall, and you need to cut costs or earn more.
draft.remember: Income minus all expenses, fixed and variable, shows what is left to save.

a.q: Mia checks what she spent on four things in March and April. Which one is a fixed cost?
opts: Music app: $12 in March, $12 in April
Myki top-up: $30 in March, $22 in April
a.why: The music app cost the same amount in both months, so it is a fixed cost. Snacks, myki top-ups and clothes went up or down between months, so they are variable costs, even though a myki is used often.
a.clue: Compare the two months for each item.

b.q: Jaden earns $200 a month from a weekend job. His fixed costs are $60 and his variable costs are $150. What does his budget show?
opts: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut costs or earn more
$10 left over, so he can save $10 a month from his job
$140 left over, because only fixed costs are counted
$50 left over, because only variable costs are counted
b.why: Total expenses are $60 + $150 = $210, which is $10 more than his income of $200, so the budget shows a shortfall. The $140 and $50 answers each subtract only one kind of cost, but a budget counts both fixed and variable costs.
b.clue: Add both kinds of cost before comparing with income.

a.best: Music app: $12 in March, $12 in April

b.best: A shortfall of $10, so he needs to cut costs or earn more
